meaning: A phone payment that moves money from your bank account straight into another person's account. Hard to get back, so pay only people you know.
clues: You use your phone to send money to another person.
The money moves straight from your bank account into theirs, with no app balance in between.
Your own bank may offer it right inside its banking app.
Payments are hard to get back, so only pay people you know.
Its name has five letters and starts with Z.
assumes: Venmo, Cash App, and PayPal keep money in an app balance

decoys.meaning: A money app for sending money to friends and paying at checkout. You choose who can see your payments.
A money app for sending money to friends and family. It also has its own debit card.
An online account for sending money or paying for things. It can use a PayPal balance or a bank account.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Try it: look in your bank's app, or go to zellepay.com, to see if your bank offers it.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Cash handed over was gone for good, so we only handed it to people we knew. That rule still holds here.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: And if someone says they're from your bank and tells you to move money, hang up. Then call your bank on a number you know is real. Your bank never asks you to move money.
